- .claude/commands/implement-plan-claude.md:12 | severity=critical | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite]
  PROBLEM: The cleanup trigger is placed within Step 0, before the plan is read in Step 1, so the Source issue identifier needed to evaluate the cleanup predicate is unavailable.
  WHY: The predicate cannot be evaluated at that point, leaving the stopped stage session unarchived.
- .claude/commands/implement-plan-claude.md:187 | severity=high | confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite]
  PROBLEM: The cleanup-section header says cleanup runs in Step 0, contradicting the issue-mode deferral.
  WHY: An unattended session may attempt cleanup before the issue identifier is available, causing a lookup failure.
- .claude/commands/implement-plan-claude.md:103, 191 | severity=high | confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite]
  PROBLEM: No failure-handling path is defined for transient set_session_title rename failures or mcp__github__issue_read label-read failures.
  WHY: A rename failure leaves the session with its old title, and a label-read failure silently skips archival, requiring manual operator cleanup despite the issue having been resumed.
- .claude/commands/implement-plan-claude.md:15, 192 | severity=low | confidence=[3]
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: When the cleanup predicate is false, the session does not log or report that cleanup was skipped.
  WHY: An operator cannot tell whether cleanup was correctly skipped, skipped unexpectedly, or ran and matched no stopped sessions.
- tests/test_implement_plan_claude_command.py:260 | severity=low | confidence=[2]
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: The title-collision check replaces the literal em-dash-prefixed suffix and then asserts the bare phrase is absent, making the check fragile to future documentation containing that phrase.
  WHY: A subsequent documentation edit containing `blocked on issue` could fail the test even though the title is still unique.
=== END CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===

=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
- .claude/commands/implement-plan-claude.md (and byte-identical twin workflow-templates/.claude/commands/implement-plan-claude.md): line 15 (Step 1 "Issue-mode resume cleanup" instruction) and line 192 (cleanup-section report line "Zombie checkers archived: <n>, plus `stopped stage sessions archived: <m>` in issue mode")
  severity=low | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: When the Step 1 instruction's predicate is false (the plan has no `Source issue:` line, or `$ARGUMENTS` carries a `— resume.` block), cleanup does not run, but the session does not log/report this skip.
  WHY: An operator reading the chat output after a `/reclarify` resume cannot tell whether (a) the resume was in project mode (no `Source issue:` line, cleanup correctly skipped), (b) the resume was in issue mode but the predicate skipped cleanup for an unexpected reason, or (c) the resume was in issue mode and cleanup ran but matched no stopped sessions. The contract test pins text presence but not a log/report line for the skip case, so this gap is silent at runtime. A one-line log directive (e.g. "report `stopped stage sessions kept: not in issue mode` when the predicate is false") would close the gap in ≤10 lines.
- tests/test_implement_plan_claude_command.py: line 260 (the assertion `assert "blocked on issue" not in text.replace("— blocked on issue", "")` inside `test_issue_mode_archives_stopped_stage_sessions`)
  severity=low | confidence=2
  PROBLEM: The title-collision check replaces the literal em-dash-prefixed suffix `— blocked on issue` and then asserts the substring `blocked on issue` (with a regular space) is not present.
  WHY: The check is fragile because it would fail on any future edit that adds explanatory documentation containing the bare phrase `blocked on issue` (with a regular space, not the em-dash prefix) — for example, a comment in the cleanup section explaining the suffix, or the plural form `blocked on issues` referenced anywhere in the command text.
- TASK_GAP
  Requirement: "When an issue-mode `/implement-plan-claude` project stops (`Status: BLOCKED`), the stage session that stopped stays open after a human answers on the issue and comments `/reclarify`. It then has to be archived by hand." plus the three numbered causes in the PR description (no `— resume.` block carries the stopped session's id; the Zombie-checker cleanup only ran from inside resume hygiene; the cleanup matched only `… — checker` / `… — waiting:` titles).
  Expected change site: .claude/commands/implement-plan-claude.md and workflow-templates/.claude/commands/implement-plan-claude.md
